aciklama: Language before theory: you can’t discuss theory until you can name a shot, a cut, a sound. This phase builds the vocabulary of analysis.

haftalar.film: Citizen Kane (Welles, 1941)
Rashomon (Kurosawa, 1950); optional Memento (Nolan, 2000)
Tokyo Story (Ozu, 1953) + Touch of Evil (Welles, 1958) opening long take
À bout de souffle (Godard, 1960) + The Conversation (Coppola, 1974)

haftalar.baslik: What is film theory? Draw the map
haftalar.film: Sherlock Jr. (Keaton, 1924)

aciklama: The central quarrel of classical theory: is what makes cinema an art its transformation of reality (the formalists, montage) or its recording of reality (the realists)? By the end of this phase you should be able to argue both sides.

haftalar.baslik: Is cinema an art? Münsterberg and Arnheim
haftalar.film: Sunrise (Murnau, 1927); Das Cabinet des Dr. Caligari (Wiene, 1920)

haftalar.baslik: The face, photogénie and the cinema of attractions
haftalar.film: Lumière short films (1895–97); Le Voyage dans la Lune (Méliès, 1902); La Passion de Jeanne d'Arc (Dreyer, 1928)

haftalar.baslik: Soviet montage I: Kuleshov, Pudovkin, Vertov
haftalar.film: Chelovek s kino-apparatom / Man with a Movie Camera (Vertov, 1929); Mat (Pudovkin, 1926)
Bronenosets Potyomkin (1925) Odessa Steps; Oktyabr (1928) “gods” sequence; modern example: The Godfather (1972) baptism sequence

haftalar.baslik: Bazin I: ontology and deep focus
haftalar.film: La Règle du jeu (Renoir, 1939); The Best Years of Our Lives (Wyler, 1946)
Ladri di biciclette (De Sica, 1948); Roma città aperta (Rossellini, 1945); Umberto D. (De Sica, 1952); for connection, Uzak (Ceylan, 2002) and Close-Up (Kiarostami, 1990)
M (Lang, 1931); Nanook of the North (Flaherty, 1922)

aciklama: Where does a film’s meaning come from: the director, the genre, the star, the studio system? This phase tests all three answers.

haftalar.baslik: Auteur I: France and Cahiers du cinéma
haftalar.film: Les Quatre Cents Coups (Truffaut, 1959); Rear Window (Hitchcock, 1954); Journal d'un curé de campagne (Bresson, 1951)

haftalar.baslik: Auteur II: America and the structuralist auteur
haftalar.film: The Searchers (Ford, 1956); Rio Bravo (Hawks, 1959); Bringing Up Baby (Hawks, 1938)

haftalar.baslik: The death of the author, and the auteur as brand
haftalar.film: The Grand Budapest Hotel (Anderson, 2014); 3 films by a director you love, over the course of this month

haftalar.baslik: Genre I: the gangster film and the western
haftalar.film: Scarface (Hawks, 1932); Stagecoach (Ford, 1939); Unforgiven (Eastwood, 1992)

haftalar.baslik: Genre II: theory, film noir, melodrama
haftalar.film: Double Indemnity (Wilder, 1944); All That Heaven Allows (Sirk, 1955); optional Chinatown (Polanski, 1974), Get Out (Peele, 2017)
Casablanca (Curtiz, 1942); Gentlemen Prefer Blondes (Hawks, 1953)

aciklama: The “grand theory” era of the 1960s–80s: can film be decoded like a language, how does it position the spectator, whose gaze does it distribute? The hardest and most important phase of the program; the texts are dense, so don’t rush.

haftalar.film: Julius Caesar (Mankiewicz, 1953); Ivan Grozny (Eisenstein, 1944)
Adieu Philippine (Rozier, 1962), which Metz breaks down into syntagmas; Psycho (Hitchcock, 1960)
The Birds (Hitchcock, 1963); Star Wars (Lucas, 1977)
Modern Times (Chaplin, 1936); Triumph des Willens (Riefenstahl, 1935), as an analysis of propaganda

haftalar.baslik: Althusser and the Cahiers critique of ideology
haftalar.film: Young Mr. Lincoln (Ford, 1939)
Week-end (Godard, 1967); Tout va bien (Godard & Gorin, 1972); 2 ou 3 choses que je sais d'elle (Godard, 1967)

La hora de los hornos (1968), part one; Deus e o Diabo na Terra do Sol (Rocha, 1964); Memorias del subdesarrollo (Gutiérrez Alea, 1968); La battaglia di Algeri (Pontecorvo, 1966); for connection, Umut (Güney, 1970)
Vertigo (Hitchcock, 1958); Persona (Bergman, 1966)
Peeping Tom (Powell, 1960); The Pervert's Guide to Cinema (Fiennes & Žižek, 2006)
Vertigo (again); Morocco (von Sternberg, 1930); Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles (Akerman, 1975)
Halloween (Carpenter, 1978); Stella Dallas (Vidor, 1937); Cléo de 5 à 7 (Varda, 1962); Portrait de la jeune fille en feu (Sciamma, 2019)

aciklama: After the 1980s, a break with grand theory in three different directions: approaching the spectator as a mind (cognitive theory), cinema as a form of thought (Deleuze), and film as bodily experience (phenomenology).

haftalar.film: Banshun / Late Spring (Ozu, 1949); Pickpocket (Bresson, 1959); Playtime (Tati, 1967)
Memento (again); Lola rennt (Tykwer, 1998); The Talented Mr. Ripley (Minghella, 1999)
Shichinin no samurai / Seven Samurai (Kurosawa, 1954); La Passion de Jeanne d'Arc (again)

haftalar.baslik: Deleuze II: crisis and the time-image
haftalar.film: Germania anno zero (Rossellini, 1948); L'avventura (Antonioni, 1960); L'Année dernière à Marienbad (Resnais, 1961)

haftalar.baslik: Deleuze III: sheets of the past and thought
haftalar.film: Zerkalo / Mirror (Tarkovsky, 1975); Bir Zamanlar Anadolu'da (Ceylan, 2011); Citizen Kane (again)
The Piano (Campion, 1993), the film with which Sobchack’s essay opens; Beau Travail (Denis, 1999)
In the Mood for Love (Wong Kar-wai, 2000); Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives (Weerasethakul, 2010); Leviathan (Castaing-Taylor & Paravel, 2012)

aciklama: Real spectators instead of theory’s “universal spectator”: how do different people read the same film, who is absent from the screen, and how does documentary construct truth?

haftalar.film: The Rocky Horror Picture Show (Sharman, 1975); The Wizard of Oz (Fleming, 1939)
Intolerance (Griffith, 1916); Star Wars (again, through the lens of fan culture)

haftalar.baslik: Race, representation and the oppositional gaze
haftalar.film: The Birth of a Nation (Griffith, 1915), viewed critically; Killer of Sheep (Burnett, 1978); Do the Right Thing (Lee, 1989); Daughters of the Dust (Dash, 1991)
La Noire de… (Sembène, 1966); Touki Bouki (Mambéty, 1973); Gegen die Wand / Head-On (Akın, 2004); Lawrence of Arabia (Lean, 1962), for a reading of Orientalism
Rope (Hitchcock, 1948); Paris Is Burning (Livingston, 1990); Happy Together (Wong Kar-wai, 1997); Lola + Bilidikid (Ataman, 1999); Carol (Haynes, 2015)
Nuit et brouillard (Resnais, 1956); Chronique d'un été (Rouch & Morin, 1961); Primary (Drew, 1960); Salesman (Maysles brothers, 1969)

The Thin Blue Line (Morris, 1988); Sans Soleil (Marker, 1983); Reassemblage (Trinh, 1982); The Act of Killing (Oppenheimer, 2012); Stories We Tell (Polley, 2012); optional: one part of Shoah (Lanzmann, 1985)

aciklama: Films are now mostly not shot on film and not watched in theaters. This phase returns to the Bazinian question from the start of the book: what is cinema once the image’s bond with reality is broken?

haftalar.film: Body Heat (Kasdan, 1981); Blue Velvet (Lynch, 1986); Blade Runner (Scott, 1982); Pulp Fiction (Tarantino, 1994); The Truman Show (Weir, 1998)

haftalar.baslik: Digital I: the crisis of the index
haftalar.film: Jurassic Park (Spielberg, 1993); The Matrix (Wachowskis, 1999); Russkiy kovcheg / Russian Ark (Sokurov, 2002); Gravity (Cuarón, 2013)
Demonlover (Assayas, 2002); Boarding Gate (Assayas, 2007); Tangerine (Baker, 2015, shot on an iPhone); Searching (Chaganty, 2018); Her (Jonze, 2013)

aciklama: Apply the theories you’ve learned to the cinema you know best. Turkey’s own theoretical debates (the national cinema quarrel) are also the subject of these two weeks.

haftalar.baslik: The national cinema debate and Yeşilçam
haftalar.film: Susuz Yaz (Erksan, 1963); Gurbet Kuşları (Refiğ, 1964); Vesikalı Yarim (Akad, 1968); Umut (Güney, 1970); Selvi Boylum Al Yazmalım (Yılmaz, 1977)
Yol (Gören & Güney, 1982); Eşkıya (Turgul, 1996); Kasaba (Ceylan, 1997); Masumiyet (Demirkubuz, 1997); Kış Uykusu (Ceylan, 2014); Mustang (Ergüven, 2015); Ahlat Ağacı (Ceylan, 2018)

aciklama: There is almost no new reading in the last four weeks; the goal is to bring what you’ve learned together into a single view and be able to defend it.

haftalar.film: 2001: A Space Odyssey (Kubrick, 1968); attractions, montage, realism and bodily experience in a single film
